question: Spring balance A is attached at one end to spring balance B, whose other end is fixed to a rigid support. A force is applied to the free end of spring balance A. Both balances show the same reading. What does this observation indicate?

options.text: The force exerted by A on B is greater than that by B on A.
The force exerted by A on B is equal and opposite to the force exerted by B on A.
Both balances exert forces in the same direction.
Only spring balance A exerts force on B.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The force exerted by A on B is equal and opposite to the force exerted by B on A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• This observation is a classic demonstration of **Newton's Third Law of Motion**, which states that for every **action**, there is an **equal and opposite reaction**.
 
• When a **force** is applied to the free end of **spring balance A**, it exerts a force on **spring balance B**. This is the **action force**. Simultaneously, spring balance B exerts a force of **equal magnitude** but in the **opposite direction** back on spring balance A. This is the **reaction force**.
 
• The fact that **both balances show the same reading** indicates that the **magnitude** of the force exerted by A on B is exactly equal to the magnitude of the force exerted by B on A. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
